key_insight: Asymmetric debate roles and evidence-based stopping make multi-agent research verification more compute-efficient while reducing role similarity and enabling auditable claim grounding.
engineering_relevance: Research-verification pipelines can use opposing agent directives, convergence monitoring, and independent evidence checks instead of fixed-round debate.
method: Assign Advocate, Skeptic, and Arbitrator roles with opposing epistemic directives.
Stop debate using the evidence-grounded Belief-Delta convergence criterion.
Anchor supported claims to verbatim literature snippets audited by an independent NLI classifier.
evidence_signal: Across 200 runs on 40 hypotheses using DeepSeek-R1-32B, the framework reported 2.4× fewer LLM calls, 0% over-iteration versus 62.5% for Fixed-3, and a 21.7% hallucination rate.
watch_item: Hallucinations remained substantial and were not significantly lower than Self-Refine's 25.9% rate (p = 0.61); generalization beyond the evaluated model and hypotheses remains unestablished.
paper_title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
